correctness.rationale: For a simplicial transposition the geometric fixed locus is the flag complex on compatible barycenters of diagonal orbits d_(a,z) and exchanged pairs p_(ab,z). The exact cross-suffix criterion permits only same-letter diagonals across suffixes or a diagonal letter incident to an exchanged pair; within one suffix every orbit pair is adjacent. Cover the core B by suffix simplices F_z and letter/suffix simplices T_(a,z); contractible intersections make the nerve theorem applicable. The described free triangle-edge collapses, then relative cone contractions retaining suffix vertices, reduce the nerve to K_(q,q), with χ=2q−q² and π1 free of rank (q−1)². Every clique outside B is a maximal bridge triangle {p_(ab,z),d_(a,w),d_(b,w)} for z≠w; there are q²(q−1)²/2 such attached two-cells, each tracing the fundamental bipartite square f_z−a−f_w−b−f_z. A chosen (q−1)² collection normally generates π1, so the full complex is simply connected and has χ=2q−q²+q²(q−1)²/2=1+Bq. A two-dimensional simply connected CW model has free H2 of rank Bq and wedge-of-2-spheres homotopy by Hurewicz/Whitehead. The thresholds 0,1,2,3 follow directly from Hamming distances, so the asserted barcode has q²−q bars [0,1), q−1 [0,2), Bq in degree 2 [2,3), plus one unreduced infinite H0 bar. Finite mod-two ranks are corroboration only.
residual_risks: The nonequivariant ambient Rips complex and the geometric fixed orbit complex cannot be conflated.

The 2D CW model is a homotopy replacement for potentially high-dimensional original flag complex; homotopy conclusion uses killing all π1 by actual square attachments, not mod-two Betti numbers alone.
